title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the sequel to La Longue Marche, Grothendieck studies the arithmetic fundamental group M (an extension 1 → 𝔊_0^+ → M → Γ_Q^~ → 1, with 𝔊_0^+ a profinite fundamental group of the base point situation for M_{0,3}/M_{0,4}). He also studies stabilizer/normaliser groups Z_{ρ0,σ0} of a pair of base 'lacets' (ρ0,σ0). On the previous page, (108) gives a homomorphism Z_{ρ0,σ0} → M[0] ≅ M̃_{0,3}[0] = M̃_{0,3}(0)·L_0^𝔖.

This page applies a general device announced in 'digressions 9°'. Call a 'system' a quadruple (Z, L ⊂ Z normal, Z → Aut(𝔊), ι: L ↪ 𝔊) satisfying the usual compatibilities:
- ι is Z-equivariant (Z acting on L by conjugation);
- L acts on 𝔊 through inner automorphisms via ι.
Such a system yields a group G = (𝔊 ⋊ Z)/{(ι(l)^{-1}, l)}. It contains 𝔊 as a normal subgroup, receives a homomorphism Z → G (injective because ι is), and sits in an extension 1 → 𝔊 → G → Z/L → 1. This is classical Schreier-type extension theory, an 'amalgamated crossed product'.

Two applications:
- (110): the system (Z_{ρ0,σ0}, L_0^♮ ⊂ Z, Z → Aut(𝔊_0^{+*}), L_0^♮ ↪ 𝔊_0^{+*}) produces (110') G_{ρ0,σ0} ⊃ 𝔊_0^{+*} with Z_{ρ0,σ0} → G_{ρ0,σ0}.
- (111): the analogous system (M[0]^♮ = M(0)·L_0^Π, L_0^⊕, M[0]^♮ → Aut(𝔊_0^+), L_0^⊕ ↪ 𝔊_0^+) reconstructs (111') the situation (M, 𝔊_0^+ ⊂ M, M[0] → M).

By (108) there is a morphism of systems (110) → (111): identity on 𝔊_0^+, (108) on Z, and the inclusion L_0^♮ ↪ L_0^⊕. By functoriality of the construction this gives a morphism (110') → (111'), in particular a morphism of exact sequences. The next page writes this out as (112): G_{ρ0,σ0} → M over γ_{ρ0,σ0} = Z/L_0^♮ → Γ_Q^~ = M[0]/L_0^𝔖. It then deduces injectivity and identifies the image with M^♮. The purpose is to realise the 'stabiliser of a pair of base lacets' group as a subgroup of the arithmetic fundamental group M, i.e. part of the comparison between Galois/GT-type automorphism groups and loop-equation stabilisers.
errors: No mathematical error is visible on this page. The construction is functorial and the claimed induced morphism of extensions is correct, provided the compatibility conditions of 9° hold for (108). Whether they do is asserted, not checked, here.
In (110') the map Z_{ρ0,σ0} → G_{ρ0,σ0} is written with a hook (injective). That is correct only because L_0^♮ → 𝔊_0^{+*} is injective, which is not restated.
Minor notational instability: 𝔊_0^{+*} in (110) versus 𝔊_0^+ in the identity statement, and 𝔊_0^{~+} on the next page.

ideas.what: Constructing a group extension 1→𝔊→G→Z/L→1 from a 'system' (Z, normal L⊂Z, action Z→Aut(𝔊), equivariant embedding L↪𝔊), namely G = (𝔊⋊Z)/L antidiagonal
ideas.modern_name: Extension from an action plus compatible embedding of a normal subgroup (Schreier extension theory / pushout of crossed modules)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Schreier, Eilenberg–MacLane); standard in anabelian geometry
ideas.where_published: Similar extension/outer-action formalism appears in SGA1 exposé on fundamental groups; specific form unsure

ideas.what: Functoriality: a morphism of systems induces a morphism of the resulting extensions, applied to compare the stabiliser group G_{ρ0,σ0} of a pair of base lacets with the arithmetic fundamental group M
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of GT-type/stabiliser groups with π_1 of M_{0,n} over Q (Ihara–Drinfeld–Grothendieck–Teichmüller setting)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990s) for GT; this specific comparison unsure
ideas.where_published: Unpublished continuation of La Longue Marche (1981)

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out routine bookkeeping: it applies a standard extension construction functorially to compare two group-theoretic situations within Grothendieck's loop-equation study. No new result or connection is visible on this page itself.
